owners.visual_integration: Scene owners choose meshes and camera anchors

purpose: One shared information layer for all scenes. Scene art, camera motion and animation remain separate.

atmospheres.label: Illustrative Earth-like cabin
atmospheres.basis: Design preset for an enclosed air-filled habitat. Not a measured Moon or Mars habitat.

atmospheres.label: Illustrative oxygen-enriched cabin
atmospheres.basis: Uses a 30% O2 / 10.2 psia atmosphere discussed in the source. Not a universal atmosphere for a planet or a safety recommendation.

materials.label: LDPE coating on NiCr core
materials.geometry: 150 mm long; 0.5 mm core diameter; 0.3 mm radial coating thickness

materials.label: Mylar G / Melinex 515
materials.geometry: 5 mil (0.127 mm) film; grade depends on test

materials.label: PMMA rods
materials.geometry: Diameter depends on investigation; do not merge configurations

cards.title: What starts a fire?
cards.summary: A fire needs fuel, oxygen and enough ignition energy.

sections.heading: Here in the galley
sections.body: The burner is an intentional ignition source. A nearby material needs enough heating to ignite; arriving on the Moon or Mars does not ignite it automatically.

sections.heading: Beyond the stove
sections.body: An electrical fault or overheating equipment can provide ignition energy in a habitat. Ventilation and gravity then affect how the fire behaves.

cards.title: The pan is our starting point
cards.summary: Use the familiar kitchen to explore fire research.

sections.heading: What this object shows
sections.body: The pan and egg connect the scene to everyday life. The research bundle does not contain an ignition or cooking model for this particular pan, coating or food.

sections.heading: Explore the evidence
sections.body: Choose a labelled material sample to see a published result, its test conditions and its source.

cards.title: A familiar object in a different environment
cards.summary: The egg is a visual demonstration, not a flammability specimen.

sections.heading: What changes
sections.body: The scene can illustrate motion at different gravity levels. It does not calculate the egg’s cooking temperature, ignition time or fire risk.

sections.heading: Where the numbers are
sections.body: Open a tested material sample for experimental oxygen limits or flame-spread measurements.

cards.title: Fuel and cabin air are different
cards.summary: The fuel supply, cabin oxygen and cabin pressure have different roles.

sections.heading: Read the right pressure
sections.body: The environment panel reports absolute cabin pressure. It is not the pressure inside this fuel container.

sections.heading: Keep the illustration clear
sections.body: This prop does not have measured tank pressure, fuel mass or remaining burn time. A decorative fill level is not a fuel calculation.

cards.title: Lower gravity still pulls objects down
cards.summary: The Moon and Mars are partial-gravity environments.

sections.heading: Motion
sections.body: Loose objects can follow slower falling arcs. Indefinite orbital-style floating is not the behaviour of unsupported objects on either surface.

sections.heading: Fire research
sections.body: The scene’s movement is an illustration. Material test results remain attached to their original gravity, atmosphere and apparatus.

cards.title: A visual part of the galley
cards.summary: This plant helps keep the scene familiar.

sections.heading: Research coverage
sections.body: The collection does not contain a flammability test for this plant, soil or pot. Open a labelled material sample to explore the fire data.

cards.title: Ultem 1000 film
cards.summary: Explore oxygen-limit tests on this specific PEI film.

sections.heading: Read the result
sections.body: The selected test lists its oxygen endpoint, pressure and apparatus. The star in ULOI* or MOC* identifies the short-duration reduced-gravity method.

sections.heading: Application
sections.body: A sample is a link to material evidence. Its result does not rate an entire stove, handle or spacecraft.

cards.title: Nomex HT90-40 fabric
cards.summary: Compare published tests on this specific fabric grade.

sections.heading: What you are selecting
sections.body: The cloth represents a labelled test specimen. It is not a claim that every kitchen towel uses Nomex.

sections.heading: Read the result
sections.body: Use the test pressure and endpoint definition beside the number. Results do not establish a safe oxygen setting for a habitat.

cards.title: LDPE-coated NiCr wire
cards.summary: Explore measured flame spread at Martian gravity.

sections.heading: What the number describes
sections.body: The study follows downward flame spread on a 150 mm wire with a 0.5 mm NiCr core and a 0.3 mm LDPE coating.

sections.heading: An observed mechanism
sections.body: Molten coating can move cyclically ahead of the flame. These attached polymer droplets are different from the free water droplets in the galley.

cards.title: PET film: check the exact grade
cards.summary: The reduced-gravity tests used Mylar G; the Earth comparison used Melinex 515.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.body: Both are PET films, but they are different product grades. Show the grade on every result. The star-marked reduced-gravity endpoints also use a different test criterion from the Earth endpoints.

cards.title: PMMA rod research
cards.summary: Rod experiments help explain how gravity and airflow affect burning.

sections.heading: Evidence available
sections.body: The collection includes BASS-II findings and LUCI fitted flame-motion measurements. Open each source with its own diameter, apparatus and metric.

sections.heading: Keep the metrics separate
sections.body: Flame-tip motion, flame-base motion and material flame-spread rate are not interchangeable. A rod result does not rate a transparent kitchen container.

cards.title: Smoke is part of the hazard
cards.summary: SAME studied the particles that spacecraft detectors need to detect.

sections.heading: What changes
sections.body: Particle sizes and composition depend on the material and conditions. Gravity and ventilation also affect how smoke reaches a detector.

sections.heading: What this panel shows
sections.body: Use a research finding about smoke, not a live cabin concentration or an invented alarm countdown.

cards.title: Equipment needs its own evidence
cards.summary: Fire suppression has different data from material flammability.

sections.heading: Research example
sections.body: NASA developed an orientation-independent fine-water-mist extinguisher and tested it against open and obstructed fires.

sections.heading: Use the correct scope
sections.body: This panel explains the published equipment work. It does not give a measured lunar or Martian extinguishing time.

cards.title: Inside an air-filled habitat
cards.summary: The destination and the cabin atmosphere are separate choices.

sections.heading: Destination
sections.body: Earth, orbital microgravity, Moon and Mars identify gravity contexts.

sections.heading: Atmosphere
sections.body: Oxygen percentage, absolute cabin pressure and ventilation describe the enclosed air. The same illustrative cabin atmosphere can be used in both surface scenes.

sections.heading: Evidence
sections.body: A selected experiment always shows its own conditions, even when they differ from the scene settings.

ULOI.label: Ground-test ULOI
ULOI.meaning: Oxygen level at which the material passed the modified ground-test burn-length criterion about half the time.

MOC.label: Ground-test MOC
MOC.meaning: Maximum oxygen concentration meeting the study’s repeated ground-test self-extinguishment criterion.

ULOI*.label: Survived the short drop
ULOI*.meaning: Lowest tested oxygen concentration where the flame survived the full drop.

MOC*.label: Extinguished during the drop
MOC*.meaning: Highest tested oxygen concentration where the flame extinguished within the drop.

flame_spread_mm_s.label: Measured flame-spread rate
flame_spread_mm_s.meaning: Downward propagation rate in the reported wire test. Not ignition time or a prediction for another object.

characteristic_time_s.label: Characteristic time
characteristic_time_s.meaning: Study-defined characteristic time, not ignition time.

ui_states.no_matching_case: No matching test in this collection

rules: Render research evidence under Published test. Never silently relabel it as the current scene result.
Changing destination changes the scene gravity and relevant case list. It does not change cabin oxygen or pressure.
A missing experiment is not proof of safety or of no research anywhere.
A material sample is not a whole-product test. Keep grade, thickness and geometry visible.
Oxygen endpoints, spread rates, flame-tip fits and smoke statistics stay in different views.
Keep null values null. Extinction is an outcome, not a measured zero spread rate.
Do not compute a risk percentage, ignition countdown, safe distance or universal material ranking.
Selecting an experiment can update the test panel. Applying its settings to a scene must be an explicit separate action.
Do not connect sparse points into a continuous lunar/Martian prediction. Display published points and their evidence types.
Li Tables 1 and 2 remain distinct; their same-stated-condition rates differ. Default to Table 1 for the oxygen comparison.
No scientific copy or numbers are embedded in the scene mesh files.
Color is paired with a text label; hover emphasis is not a calculated burning warning.

details.limitation: Lunar buoyant velocity is undetermined; model uses conservative assumptions. Source reports unexplained disagreement with some lunar tests; not an approved qualification standard. Smolder is a surface reaction, outside gas-phase blowoff model assumptions.

findings.statement: For silicone rubber smoke, the arithmetic mean particle diameter was about 227 nm, while almost half the aerosol mass was in particles larger than 1000 nm. A small average size can hide a large share of the smoke mass in bigger particles.
findings.limitations: Literature finding, not a single run. Not an alarm threshold for a habitat.

findings.statement: Materials were heated below ignition; smoke aging ranged 10-1800 s; a substantial portion of particles were below 500 nm. The source smoke-transport model indicates mixing-dominated transport and longer detection delays than under normal gravity.
BASS-II estimated heat release from oxygen consumption using 13.1 kJ per gram of O2; most reported tests were below 100 W.
findings.limitations: Study method and aggregate finding; not a per-test value.

findings.statement: A NASA assessment approved in March 2022 and published in May 2026 reports ISS water-mist and Orion water-spray extinguisher certification at 30% O2 and 10.2 psia. It identifies lower-pressure discharge and higher-oxygen effectiveness concerns. This does not establish qualification at lunar gravity.

NASA's orientation-independent water/nitrogen fine-water-mist extinguisher, rechargeable from onboard supplies, succeeded against open and baffled-enclosure fires in proof-of-concept tests. Potential Earth uses include aircraft and overturned vehicles.

Some materials that do not sustain burning at 1g can burn in microgravity with low-speed flow or in partial gravity. Earlier work suggests a flame-spread peak and minimum oxygen for burning near lunar gravity for certain cases.
findings.limitations: Condition-specific; not a universal curve. Neither paper supports 'Moon is always worst'.

findings.statement: LUCI used an 11-rpm rotating New Shepard vehicle (effective radius 1.22 m) to burn cotton/fiberglass and a 4-mm PMMA rod in air at normal pressure for over 2.5 minutes.
findings.limitations: Coriolis effects; not a lunar-surface test.

findings.title: Earth tests can miss some low-gravity burning conditions
findings.body: BASS-II reported sustained burning of a quarter-inch PMMA rod at 13.6% oxygen in microgravity, compared with a 16% Earth-gravity blowoff limit. The difference is 2.4 percentage points for this rod experiment.
findings.scope: Evidence card only. Different reported endpoints; this is not a universal PMMA threshold or a lunar safety rating. Source slides do not supply the full paired conditions.
